summary:
I've been building out a fleet monitoring platform (intranet-dashboard) that watches four machines — a GPU box, two dev servers, and a media server. It started as agentless: an SSH collector ships as a plain script over stdin each cycle, no agent installed anywhere, and lands everything in SQLite with a retention ladder (raw for a week, five-minute buckets for three months, hourly after that, always keeping min/max so a spike doesn't get smoothed away). I added GPU and CPU power tracking to it recently by reading each card's power draw and the CPU's RAPL counters directly rather than estimating from load — which mattered, because the estimate-based numbers I'd been using for months on my AI desktop were off in ways I couldn't see until I had ground truth to compare against.

That desktop also went down hard for a couple of days — no POST, no boot, just a dead machine. No crash logs to work from, since it lost power before it could write anything. I ended up narrowing it to the power supply by elimination: ran it through a soak test with the load ramped up and down repeatedly, then a GPU burst to full rated draw, checked every log source that could show a fault (thermal, memory errors, PCIe), and it came back clean everywhere except the one component the swap fixed. It's back up and I built the harness so I don't have to reconstruct that process from scratch next time.

On the product side, I've been shipping features for TheLongRest, a D&D campaign app I built and use to actually run games with friends. The one I'm proudest of: import a published adventure module, and it derives dungeon-master prep from the text — NPCs, locations, encounter beats — without ever storing the source material itself, since I don't have rights to redistribute it. Everything that survives is what the DM chose to keep, in their own words. I dogfooded it prepping a real one-shot for my group, which surfaced a batch of rough edges (an AI classifier over-flagging plot secrets as spoiled, some formatting quirks from how the import tool handled book text) that got fixed before the session.
